description:
FILED s421 (Fable review of s420).  Umbrella like #415; close items
INDIVIDUALLY by editing this list.  All three measured at 0 rows in the
corpora; they are recorded so nobody re-derives them.

1. `"@{^CAPTURE}"` and `"@{^CAPTURE}[0]"` INSIDE a dq string are DROPPED
   ("Bug. Fell through. Missing case"); `"$#{^CAPTURE}"` (fixed by #412),
   `"${^CAPTURE}[1]"` and every list-context form work.  StringInterpolation's
   `@{` path does not know a caret name; perl interpolates it ("a b").
   Same file as #420 — take them together if #420 is done locally.

2. `$Ｘ {a}` — whitespace between a repaired non-ASCII symbol and its
   subscript: `_reclass_subscripts_after` (Pl/Parser.pm, #410) stops at the
   Whitespace sibling, so the `{a}` stays a BLOCK and `$Ｘ` is read as the
   SCALAR `$Ｘ` (unbound-variable crash at load).  ASCII `$x {a}` works (PPI
   itself lexes that as a Subscript), so mirror PPI: step over whitespace
   (`snext_sibling`), and probe that `for my $Ｘ (...) {` is untouched (its
   next significant sibling is `(`, not a container).

3. PPI's LEXER fails the WHOLE document on a non-ASCII foreach loop variable:
   `for my $Ｉ (1,2) { 1 }`, `foreach my $Ｉ (...)`, `for $Ｉ (...)`,
   `for my $Ｉ(...)`, `for my $Ｉ (@a)` → "Lexer failed: Illegal state in
   'foreach' compound statement" (PPI 1.291), so PCL dies "PPI failed to
   tokenize" and the file is lost.  `for (my $Ｉ=0; ...)`, `while (my $Ｉ =
   ...)` and `my $Ｉ = 1;` lex fine.  Same root as §23 (the `$` branch of
   Unknown.pm splits `$Ｉ` into Cast + Word, and the foreach-slot state
   machine then sees a Cast where it wants a Symbol).  NO token-level
   workaround exists (the failure is before tokens); a fix would be a
   `_preprocess_source` rename of non-ASCII identifiers, which is its own
   design.  Logged as docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §23 addendum + a
   docs/ppi-bug-report.t row (s421).  Corpus: only t/lib/warnings/pad (a
   data file) carries the shape.

ITEM 1 DONE s426 (Opus), with #388 consumer 3.  `@{^NAME}` is the magic
ARRAY of that name — the symmetric twin of _scan_braced_dollar's ${^NAME}
arm, which Pl::InterpScan was missing, so the whole thing fell to form
'expr' and the consumer tried to parse `^CAPTURE` as an expression ("Bug.
Fell through. Missing case: []", a whole-statement DROP).  Probed while
adding it: like every braced NAME it CLOSES the reference —
`"@{^CAPTURE}[0]"` is the array then a literal `[0]` (perl: "a b[0]"), the
same rule `"${^CAPTURE}[1]"` follows.  `@{+}` / `@{-}` take the same arm.
Guard: Pl/t/interp-chained-subscript-01.t row 12.
ITEMS 2 and 3 REMAIN (agent F / the PPI lexer).

ITEM 2 DONE s427 (Opus).  `_reclass_subscripts_after` walked the postfix chain
with next_sibling, so ONE Whitespace token stopped it and the LEXER's
bareword-derived guess stood.  The cost is not a drop, it is SILENT WRONG:
`print $Ｘ {a}` came out as `(p-print :fh |$x| "a")` — a block-form FILEHANDLE
spec — and `print $Ｖ [1]` as an anonymous array constructor.

snext_sibling is the fix, and PPI's own lexer is the specification: the ASCII
`$h {a}` and `@h {qw(a b)}` dump as PPI::Structure::Subscript under 1.291, so
the repair now decides what PPI would have decided had it seen a whole symbol.
Probed identical to perl: `$Ｘ {a}`, `$Ｖ [1]`, `@Ｘ {qw(a b)}`, `$ｒ ->{a}`,
and the shapes it must NOT touch — `if ($Ｖ [0]) { … }`, `map { … } @Ｖ`,
`foreach (@Ｖ) { }`, a bare block, an anon sub, a `sort { }` comparator, an
anonymous hash in a list.  As the task predicted, `for my $Ｉ (…) { }` cannot
be probed at all: PPI's LEXER fails the whole document (item 3).  corpus-diff
IDENTICAL, gate-SET scan over both populations shows no verdict moving for
this item.  Guard Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t row 8.

ITEM 3 REMAINS (the PPI lexer; upstream, already logged as §23's addendum).
title: s421 review-probe residues (small, each its own spelling): "@{^CAPTURE}" interpolation drops; `$Ｘ {a}` after a repaired non-ASCII symbol; PPI's LEXER fails a file on a non-ASCII foreach variable
